message: skipped feature with empty geometry
help: Filter empty-geometry features upstream or fix the source data.

message: skipped schema feature missing the configured schemaKey attribute
help: Ensure upstream features carry the attribute named by schemaKey, or unset schemaKey.

message: skipped feature with non-CityGML geometry
help: Cesium 3D Tiles Writer only accepts CityGML geometry; route other geometry types to a different writer.

message: left out an attribute that could not be written as a CityGML 2.0 property
help: Give the attribute a CityGML 2.0 property name of the feature's class as prefix:name; geometry property names and flattened keys are never written, and an ADE property such as uro: needs its ADE listed in adeSchemas. Read gen: attributes and coded values with keepAttributes on, so names are kept and each _code entry matches one value.

message: left out values beyond the number the CityGML 2.0 schema allows
help: The property allows fewer values than the attribute holds; most allow one. Keep only the values to write.

message: could not copy a codelist beside the output; its original URL was written instead
help: Check that the codelist the reader recorded under the attribute's _codeSpace key is still readable where the workflow runs.

message: skipped feature with no geometry for the configured LOD mask
help: Check the feature's LODs against the writer's LOD configuration.

message: left out an element or XML attribute that had no value
help: An element is written only with a value or a child element, so an empty string writes nothing, as does an element with only XML attributes such as uom or codeSpace; one holding only an xlink:href reference is still written. An element an empty value leaves without a part its schema requires, such as a generic attribute without gen:value or an address without core:xalAddress, is left out whole, and an empty XML attribute is left off its element. Fill the value upstream, or remove the attribute before the writer.

message: left geometry out of a feature because its class declares no property for that LOD and geometry type
help: The feature's CityGML class declares no property for that LOD and geometry type, and no lodNGeometry for that LOD to hold it instead, so that geometry was skipped and the rest of the feature written. Set the feature's source property name to one the class declares, change the geometry's LOD, or change the feature type to a class that declares such a property.

message: dropped lod1MultiSurface from an object that also carries lod1Solid
help: CityGML 2.0 allows only one of lod1Solid and lod1MultiSurface, and defines them as identical at LOD1. Supply just one of the two.

message: the document is well-formed XML but contains content that cannot be read
help: The read's error message names the file and what could not be read, such as a coordinate list or an xlink:href, with the element's gml:id where one is available; correct that content in the source file.

message: left out a nested city object, such as a boundary surface
help: Nested city objects such as bldg:boundedBy and bldg:consistsOfBuildingPart are not written yet; their geometry is still written onto the parent object.

message: skipped feature with non-CityGML geometry
help: CityGML Writer only writes CityGML geometry; route other geometry types to a different writer.

message: the document could not be parsed as the reader's CityGML version
help: Check that the file is well-formed UTF-8 XML and that its CityGML version matches the reader; a 3.0 document needs the CityGML 3 version of the reader, a 2.0 document the CityGML 2 version.

message: wrote a feature as gen:GenericCityObject because its feature type names no CityGML class
help: Give the feature type as a class's qualified name, such as bldg:Building or uro:UndergroundBuilding, or a CityGML 2.0 class name alone, such as Building. A name found in several modules, such as WallSurface or Door, needs its prefix. An ADE class needs its ADE listed in adeSchemas.

message: the file contained no data rows
help: Check the file path, and check the header row settings if the file does have data.

message: skipped feature with no drawable geometry
help: CZML draws points, lines and faces. A feature with no geometry, or one carrying only point-cloud or unevaluated CSG data, has nothing the writer can draw.

message: skipped geocentric packet because force2D was requested
help: EPSG:4978 has no 2D form and dropping Z from an ECEF coordinate is meaningless, not merely lossy. Turn force2D off, or supply the positions as `cartographicDegrees`.

message: skipped packet whose cartesian position is in an inertial reference frame
help: `referenceFrame: "INERTIAL"` is not earth-fixed, so it cannot be placed without a time. Convert the positions to the FIXED frame before reading.

message: skipped feature without a feature_id
help: Ensure upstream features carry a CityGML gml:id before reaching the CZML Writer.

message: skipped feature with non-CityGML geometry
help: CZML Writer only converts CityGML geometry to polygons; route other geometry types to a different writer.

message: skipped feature with more faces than the writer will emit
help: Each face becomes its own CZML entity, so a finely tessellated surface such as a terrain mesh produces an unusably large file. Simplify or split the geometry before the CZML Writer.

message: skipped feature whose coordinates cannot be placed on the globe
help: CZML positions are longitude, latitude and height on the WGS84 globe, so the writer needs to know what coordinate system the feature is in. Reproject it, or set its CRS, before the CZML Writer.

message: skipped packet with a position this reader cannot interpret
help: Interval-scoped property arrays, `reference`/`references` positions and time-tagged `cartesian` positions are not read yet. Use a static `cartographicDegrees`, `cartographicRadians` or `cartesian` value.

message: skipped attribute operation that failed to evaluate
help: Check the operation's expression for the attribute it reads or produces.

message: expression evaluation failed
help: Check the expression for this parameter. A common cause is referencing an attribute that does not exist on the incoming feature — verify the attribute name, and that an upstream action produces it.

message: area is in square degrees, not a real-world area
help: Check your input geometry's coordinate system and reproject it to a projected CRS; a geographic CRS measures area in degrees, not a real-world unit.

message: geometry parts sit in different coordinate frames, so the summed area mixes units
help: Reproject all parts of the geometry to a single coordinate system before measuring area.

message: area not measurable, wrote 0
help: An unevaluated CSG tree is the one geometry Area Calculator cannot measure; run CSG Evaluator to compute the solid it describes, then measure the result.

message: skipped geometry part(s) that cannot be measured; their area is not in the total
help: An unevaluated CSG tree is the one geometry part that cannot be measured; run CSG Evaluator on the geometry before measuring so that every part counts toward the total.

message: cannot establish the coordinate system's unit, so the area's unit is unknown
help: Check your input geometry's coordinate system; Area Calculator could not determine whether it measures in a linear or an angular unit.

message: skipped feature in a different coordinate frame than the node's other inputs
help: Reproject every input of the node to one coordinate frame upstream.

message: rejected an extrusion with no volume or area
help: Check the height and direction values, which must give a non-zero length and a flat top above every base vertex. Check the geometry too: a face needs three distinct vertices and a line two, every ring of a face with holes must enclose some area, and no face or edge may lie parallel to the extrusion or be collapsed by a flattened base or flat top.

message: rejected a geometry that cannot be extruded: non-finite coordinates, or a surface that has no area, has self-crossing rings or a hole out of its face's plane, or is closed, non-manifold, non-orientable or not planar
help: Remove NaN or infinite coordinates and surfaces with no area upstream, and validate or repair the rest: each hole must lie in its face's plane. A surface-normal extrusion also needs a planar surface.

message: rejected a feature whose extrusion value is missing, not a finite number, or not an [x, y, z] array
help: Fill or filter features whose height, elevation, distance or vector is null, not a number, or not an [x, y, z] array.

message: rejected a feature whose coordinate system cannot support this extrusion
help: Reproject to a known projected coordinate system upstream with Coordinate Frame Reprojector. Vector and surface-normal extrusions need linear units; any extrusion of an area needs a coordinate system whose axes are known; and a face with holes that is too close to a pole (within a degree of it), crosses the antimeridian or circles a pole cannot be oriented in a geographic coordinate system.

message: rejected a feature whose geometry type cannot be extruded in this direction
help: Solids, CSG trees and point clouds cannot be extruded, a feature with no geometry gets this code too, and a point or line has no surface normal. Filter those features out, or choose the vertical or vector direction.

message: skipped feature whose horizontal footprint could not be computed
help: Planar tests compare 3D geometry by its footprint; check that the geometry is a supported, non-degenerate solid or surface.

message: skipped feature whose parts are in different coordinate frames
help: Reproject the geometry to one coordinate frame upstream.

message: skipped feature mixing 2D and 3D parts
help: Split the geometry, or force it to a single dimension upstream.

message: failed every candidate because no supplied filter geometry could be prepared
help: Every feature supplied as a filter was rejected, so there was nothing left to test against; the preceding warnings name the cause. Reproject all inputs of the node to one coordinate frame in linear units upstream.

message: skipped 3D feature in a coordinate frame without linear units
help: Reproject 3D input to a coordinate system in linear units upstream.

message: skipped feature whose spatial relationship test failed
help: Check that the geometry is valid and in a frame the predicate can test.

message: skipped solid with zero faces
help: The solid has no renderable faces; check upstream geometry processing.

message: dividing on a grid measured in degrees
help: Cell size is in the units of the data's coordinate system. In a geographic system that means degrees, so a cell size of 1.0 is roughly 111 km. Reproject to a projected coordinate system first if you meant metres.

message: skipped feature whose parts are in different coordinate systems
help: Grid Divider lays one grid over a whole feature, so every part of it must share a coordinate system. Reproject the parts to a single system before dividing.

message: skipped feature that could not be divided
help: Grid Divider divides surfaces: polygons, polygon meshes and triangular meshes. A feature is skipped when it has no area to cut into cells, when the grid itself is unusable, or when a divided piece could not be rebuilt. Read the `_grid_error` attribute on the skipped feature for the specific cause.

message: additional diagnostics collapsed into this overflow marker
help: The run produced more warnings than the summary shows. Fix the highest-count warnings first to reduce the tail.

message: internal invariant violated
help: This is an engine bug. Please report it with the workflow, the failing node, and the job id.

message: node failed with an unclassified error
help: See the message and the failing action's log for details. If it points at a workflow parameter or input, fix that and retry.

message: skipped feature whose mesh code could not be computed
help: Reprojecting the feature or intersecting it with the mesh failed. Check that the coordinate system is a valid EPSG code and that the geometry is valid.

message: skipped feature whose parts are in different coordinate systems
help: One mesh code is assigned to a whole feature, so every part of it must share a coordinate system. Reproject the parts to a single system first.

message: skipped feature with no coordinate reference system
help: Mesh codes are defined on latitude and longitude, so the feature's coordinate system must be known. Set it on the reader or with a reprojector first.

message: skipped feature that cannot be measured in its coordinate system
help: Largest overlap compares areas in square metres or lengths in metres, so a surface or line must be in a projected coordinate system in metres. Reproject it first, or choose a representative point as the location. Point features are accepted in any coordinate system.

message: skipped feature that overlaps no mesh by a measurable amount
help: Overlaps are rounded to two decimal places, so a feature whose overlap with every mesh is under 0.005 square metres (areas) or 0.005 metres (lengths) measures zero. Choose a representative point as the location for very small features.

message: skipped feature outside the range covered by Japanese mesh codes
help: Japanese standard mesh codes cover latitudes from 0 up to (not including) about 66.67 degrees and longitudes from 100 up to (not including) 200 degrees. Check that the feature's coordinate system is set correctly.

message: skipped 3D feature for largest overlap
help: Largest overlap measures a flat footprint. Flatten the feature first, with Footprint Replacer for surfaces or Two Dimension Forcer, or choose a representative point as the location.

message: skipped feature with no usable geometry
help: The feature has no geometry, or a geometry with no position to read, such as a point cloud or an unevaluated boolean solid. Largest overlap also needs a feature that is wholly 2D or wholly 3D, so a collection mixing 2D and 3D parts is skipped: flatten it with Footprint Replacer first, or choose a representative point as the location.

message: feature left out of a tile at the highest zoom level to keep the tile under the maximum tile size
help: Raise Maximum Tile Size (measured before compression) or Maximum Zoom on the MVT Writer, or write fewer attributes. The tile is first coarsened, then its smallest features are thinned out.

message: failed to save the rasterized image
help: Check that the configured save path is writable.

message: skipped assigning texture coordinates to a feature
help: Image Rasterizer only assigns texture coordinates to CityGML geometry with a non-degenerate boundary.

message: kept a value as-is because it could not be parsed as the target type
help: Check that the source attribute's value matches the int or float format expected by the extract rule.

message: kept a value as-is because it was not a string
help: Attribute Table Extractor can only coerce string values to int or float. Check the source attribute's type.
